angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 163,281 km at 69.20 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 14.4506 +/- 0.0269 mas (same row, RUWE 1.14): 69.20 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.2347 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Barkaoui et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4184 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..38B/abstract): 163,281 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.2109 +/- 0.029 solar masses from Barkaoui et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4184 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..38B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3238 +/- 48 K from Barkaoui et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4184 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..38B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barkaoui et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4184 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..38B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4184.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.021, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4184 (pscomppars): spectral type M5.5+/-0.5, from Barkaoui et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..38B/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4184 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.27 dex, from Barkaoui et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..38B/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4184 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -2.2644, from Barkaoui et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..38B/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4184 (pscomppars): age 6.7 Gyr, from Barkaoui et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..38B/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
